In a game there are n players. After the game there will be hand shaking between all pairs of players.
So we have to find how many hand shakes take place.

using System;
using System.Linq;
using System.IO;
using System.Text;
using System.Collections;
using System.Collections.Generic;

/**
 * Auto-generated code below aims at helping you parse
 * the standard input according to the problem statement.
 **/
class Solution
{
    static void Main(string[] args)
    {
        int n = int.Parse(Console.ReadLine());

        Console.WriteLine(n * (n - 1) / 2);
    }
}




Write a program that prints the numbers from 1 to N except for multiples of 5 where you have to print "Foo" and for the multiples of 7 where you have to print "Bar". For numbers which are multiples of both 5 and 7 print "FooBar".

using System;
using System.Linq;
using System.IO;
using System.Text;
using System.Collections;
using System.Collections.Generic;

/**
 * Auto-generated code below aims at helping you parse
 * the standard input according to the problem statement.
 **/
class Solution
{
    static void Main(string[] args)
    {
        int N = int.Parse(Console.ReadLine());

        for (int i = 1; i <= N; i++)
        {
            if (i%5 == 0 && i%7!=0)
            {
                Console.WriteLine("Foo");
            }
            else if (i%7==0 && i%5!=0)
            {
                Console.WriteLine("Bar");
            }
            else if (i%5==0 && i%7==0)
            {
                Console.WriteLine("FooBar");
            }
            else
            {
                Console.WriteLine(i);
            }
        }
    }
}


The game mode is REVERSE: You do not have access to the statement. You have to guess what to do by observing the following set of tests:
01 Test 1
Input
Expected output
3
Alice
Bob
Charlie
Alice Bob
Bob Charlie
Charlie Alice

using System;
using System.Linq;
using System.IO;
using System.Text;
using System.Collections;
using System.Collections.Generic;

/**
 * Auto-generated code below aims at helping you parse
 * the standard input according to the problem statement.
 **/
class Solution
{
    static void Main(string[] args)
    {
        int N = int.Parse(Console.ReadLine());
        List<string> PLAYER = new List<string>();

        for (int i = 0; i < N; i++)
        {
            PLAYER.Add(Console.ReadLine());
        }

        for (int i = 0; i < N; i++)
        {
            string fir = PLAYER[i];
            string sec = PLAYER[(i + 1) % N];

            Console.WriteLine($"{fir} {sec}");
        }
    }
}


INPUT:
A string number which contains a hexadecimal number in capitals.

OUTPUT:
The decimal value of the given number.

CONSTRAINTS:
number represents a positive integer ≤ 10000000.

EXAMPLE:
Input
F
Output
15
using System;
using System.Linq;
using System.IO;
using System.Text;
using System.Collections;
using System.Collections.Generic;

/**
 * Auto-generated code below aims at helping you parse
 * the standard input according to the problem statement.
 **/
class Solution
{
    static void Main(string[] args)
    {
        string number = Console.ReadLine();

         dec = Convert.ToInt32(number, 16);

        Console.WriteLine(dec);
    }
}


The game mode is REVERSE: You do not have access to the statement. You have to guess what to do by observing the following set of tests:
01 Test 1
Input
Expected output
5
2
2
using System;
using System.Linq;
using System.IO;
using System.Text;
using System.Collections;
using System.Collections.Generic;

/**
 * Auto-generated code below aims at helping you parse
 * the standard input according to the problem statement.
 **/
class Solution
{
    static void Main(string[] args)
    {
        int N = int.Parse(Console.ReadLine());
        int M = int.Parse(Console.ReadLine());

        if (M == 0) 
        {
            Console.WriteLine(0);
        }
        else 
        {
            Console.WriteLine(N / M);
        }


    }
} 


A warrior is fighting a slime boss. The health of the slime boss is H.

On each turn, the warrior can attack a slime. When a slime is attacked, the following happens:
- If the slime's health is 1, it disappears.
- If the slime's health is X, which is greater than 1, it splits into two slimes with health X/2, rounded down.

The warrior wins when all the slimes have disappeared. Find the number of attacks they need to use before winning.
Input
Line 1: An integer H: the initial health of the slime boss.
Output
Line 1: The number of attacks the warrior needs to use before winning.
Constraints
1 ≤ H ≤ 10⁶
using System;
using System.Linq;
using System.IO;
using System.Text;
using System.Collections;
using System.Collections.Generic;

/**
 * Auto-generated code below aims at helping you parse
 * the standard input according to the problem statement.
 **/
class Solution
{
    static void Main(string[] args)
    {
        int H = int.Parse(Console.ReadLine());

        Console.WriteLine(Attacks(H));
    }
    static int Attacks(int h)
    {
        
        if (h == 1)
            return 1;

    
        return 1 + 2 * Attacks(h / 2);
    }
}
